title: Internet Identity role-based access with auto-created users (default Employee) and admin role management

requirements.text: Replace the current “Internet Identity + credential login session” gate with an “Internet Identity only” gate: after a successful Internet Identity sign-in, the app must enter the main application without showing the CredentialLoginPage, and the app must determine access from a role stored in the backend keyed by the caller’s principal.

quotes: just to clarify can the flow be: • User signs in with Internet Identity • Your backend receives their principal • Your backend checks: “everyone will be their principal defauld mode: Employee” automatically assign a default role  as: employee. Untill me, in the settings side, I can see their ID and change it into: Manager or keep as employee. • Then your app shows pages based on that role

acceptanceCriteria: When signed in with Internet Identity, the app does not redirect to or render CredentialLoginPage.
The app’s route guards (e.g., RequireRole) use the backend role associated with the caller’s principal (not the credential session).
Logging out ends the Internet Identity session (or returns to the Internet Identity login screen) and clears cached role-protected data.

requirements.text: Implement backend user-role persistence keyed by principal ID with automatic first-login provisioning: when a principal is seen for the first time, the backend must create a user record with default role = employee (non-admin) and return that role for subsequent calls.

quotes: everyone will be their principal defauld mode: Employee automatically assign a default role as: employee

acceptanceCriteria: For a principal that has never been seen before, the first role fetch returns employee and persists it for subsequent role fetches.
For an existing principal, the stored role is returned consistently across calls.
Backend authorization checks that rely on roles continue to function using the stored role (i.e., the caller is treated as a user/employee after first login provisioning).

requirements.text: Add backend admin APIs to support owner/admin role management over principals: provide an admin-only method to list users (at minimum: principal ID + current role) and an admin-only method to change a user’s role between employee and manager/admin as supported by the app’s role enum.

quotes: Untill me, in the settings side, I can see their ID and change it into: Manager or keep as employee.

acceptanceCriteria: A non-admin caller cannot list users or change roles (backend rejects with an authorization error).
An admin can retrieve a list of known principals with their current roles.
An admin can update a target principal’s role, and subsequent role checks reflect the new role.

requirements.text: Update the Settings page to manage Internet Identity users by principal: display a table of known users (principal ID in monospace + current role), and provide an admin-only UI control to change a user’s role and save it via the new backend API.

quotes: in the settings side, I can see their ID and change it into: Manager or keep as employee.

acceptanceCriteria: Settings no longer shows mock employee credential data or mock alerts about a simplified credential system for this flow.
The Settings table loads from the backend list-users API and displays principal IDs and roles.
Changing a user’s role in the UI calls the backend update-role API and refreshes the table to show the new role.
Only admins can access Settings (existing route guard remains effective with the new role system).

requirements.text: Align navigation visibility and route protection with the principal-based role system: AppShell navigation filtering and RequireRole checks must use the same role source (the backend-stored role for the caller principal) and reliably hide admin-only pages (e.g., Master Data, Settings) from non-admin users.

quotes: Then your app shows pages based on that role

acceptanceCriteria: Non-admin users cannot see admin-only nav items and receive an access-denied screen if they manually navigate to admin-only routes.
Admin users can see and access admin-only routes.
Role-dependent UI updates correctly after a role change (e.g., after promoting a user, admin-only nav items appear without a hard refresh once queries are invalidated/refetched).

requirements.text: If adding new stable state for principal->role storage requires an upgrade-safe migration, create/update the backend migration logic according to the project’s conditional migration policy so existing canister data is preserved across upgrades.
acceptanceCriteria: Upgrading the canister preserves pre-existing persisted data (e.g., existing profiles/records).
After upgrade, existing principals can still fetch their roles and continue to use the app without data loss.

constraints: Backend must remain a single Motoko actor with all logic in backend/main.mo (no additional backend services).

Do not edit frontend immutable paths: frontend/src/hooks/useInternetIdentity.ts, frontend/src/hooks/useInternetIdentity.tsx, frontend/src/hooks/useActor.ts, frontend/src/main.tsx, and anything under frontend/src/components/ui (compose instead).
Use English for any user-facing UI text added/changed.
nonGoals: Do not attempt to derive email, name, or other personal identifiers from Internet Identity.
Do not implement username/password authentication as the primary login mechanism for roles (roles must be based on principal ID).
No third-party authentication providers beyond Internet Identity.
